question: Estimate the unchanged five historical permutation tails at useful resolution after a sparse pilot.
evaluation_unit: shared multiset permutations measured on five fixed statistics, regenerated independently in Python
null: uniform permutations of the original 97-letter multiset, with replacement; cribs remain fixed
rng: SplitMix64 and rejection-based bounded Fisher-Yates, as frozen in docs/statistics-conventions.md
statistics: KRYPTOS crib circular distance sum <= observed
repeated-plaintext distances strictly below five >= observed
inference: (r+1)/(N+1), marginal approximate Wilson 95% intervals, Bonferroni correction over five only
precision_rule: If any tail count < 100, register independent 1000000-sample precision run with a different seed; no pooling or within-run stopping.
falsification_criterion: Any Rust/Python histogram, observed statistic, prefix or RNG-state mismatch or C fixture mismatch fails. Published reciprocal rates are approximate comparisons, not forced targets.
limitations: Fixed historically selected statistics only; no global width/alphabet selection correction.
Permutation null does not identify cipher families.
New implementations by same coordinator, not fresh-context A7 review.
